required_actions: Do not act right away and do not buy the gift cards (critical)
Call the grandson at a number you already have, not one the caller gave (critical)
Check with another trusted family member even though the caller asked for secrecy (critical)
Report the scam to the FTC at www.ftc.gov/complaint
unsupported_claims: 'Don't buy anything and don't read out any numbers, however upsetting the story is' -> 'resist the urge to act immediately' supports 'don't buy anything'; 'don't read out any numbers' is not on the page, which gives no guidance on sharing codes or card numbers.
'you can report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov' -> this address appears only in the site menu; the article's own reporting instruction gives www.ftc.gov/complaint.
reasons: The 'read out any numbers' instruction is not on the cited page, and the report address differs from the one the cited article gives.
fix: Step 1 becomes: "Don't buy anything right away. Resist the urge to act immediately, no matter how dramatic the story may be." Delete "and don't read out any numbers, however upsetting the story is". In the closing line, replace "ReportFraud.ftc.gov" with "www.ftc.gov/complaint". Keep steps 2 and 3 and the other lines.

required_actions: Pay by credit card when you can, because card payments can be disputed (critical)
Send a dispute letter so it reaches the card company within 60 days of the date the first bill showing the error was mailed (critical)
Do not buy from a seller who insists on gift cards, wire transfers, payment apps, or cryptocurrency (critical)
Look for https at the start of the web address, knowing it means the connection is encrypted and does not prove the seller is honest
unsupported_claims: 'Call your card company right away, and send a letter so it reaches them within 60 days' -> the 60-day letter rule is on the page, but the page does not tell the user to call the card company.
reasons: The instruction to call the card company is not on the cited article; the letter rule is supported.
fix: In step 1, delete "Call your card company right away, and" so the sentence reads: "If a charge is wrong, you can dispute it. Send a letter so it reaches your card company within 60 days of the date the first bill showing the error was mailed." Optionally change "the connection is private" in step 3 to "the connection is encrypted" to match the page. Keep the rest.

required_actions: Do not send the code; a verification code is only for you to log in (critical)
Block the sender's number and stop texting them (critical)
Call the bank using a number from your statement or the bank's app, not the number in the text (critical)
Report the text at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
unsupported_claims: 'Block the number if you know how. If not, just ignore it.' -> the page says 'Block their number. Stop texting them.' It does not say to ignore the text.

'If you already sent the code, call your bank right away ... and tell them what happened.' -> the page says to contact the bank using a number you trust, but it does not say 'right away' or to tell the bank what happened, and it does not address a code already shared.
reasons: Two sentences go beyond the cited FTC page: the 'just ignore it' fallback and the 'call right away / tell them what happened' instruction for a code already sent.
fix: Step 2 becomes: "Block their number and stop texting them." (delete the 'If not, just ignore it' sentence). In the closing paragraph, replace "call your bank right away using a phone number from your bank statement or your bank's app and tell them what happened" with "contact your bank using a phone number from your bank statement or your bank's app". Keep steps 1, 3 and 4.
